pairs.question: Can I use quit medications if I'm pregnant?
pairs.answer: No, these products should not be used by pregnant or nursing women. It's important to talk to your healthcare provider for more information.
pairs.evidence: These products should not be used by pregnant or nursing women, people under 18 and people with other medical conditions.

pairs.question: When is the hardest time after quitting?
pairs.answer: The first seven to 10 days are the toughest, and you may need the most help during these early days. It's a critical time for your quitting journey.
pairs.evidence: The first seven to 10 days are the toughest, and you may need the most help during these early days.

pairs.question: How long do most people take to quit for good?
pairs.answer: Most people who smoke and use tobacco products return to doing so within the first three months. It's important to keep trying and not give up.
pairs.evidence: Most people who smoke and use tobacco products return to doing so within the first three months.

pairs.question: What if I feel like giving up?
pairs.answer: As long as you keep trying and don't give up, you will be able to quit for good. Remember, every attempt is a step closer to success.
pairs.evidence: As long you keep trying and don't give up, you will be able to quit for good.

pairs.question: What should I do if I slip up while trying to quit smoking?
pairs.answer: A slip does not mean you're starting over. As long as you keep trying and don't give up, you will be able to quit for good.
pairs.evidence: A slip does not mean you're starting over. As long you keep trying and don't give up, you will be able to quit for good.

pairs.question: Is it normal to have urges to smoke after quitting?
pairs.answer: Yes, it's normal to get urges to use tobacco months or even years after quitting. These urges will occur less often over time and they'll eventually stop completely.
pairs.evidence: People who formerly used tobacco products sometimes get urges to use months or even years after they quit. This is normal. These urges will occur less often over time and they'll eventually stop completely.

pairs.question: What can I do to stay quit if I face challenges?
pairs.answer: Making plans to meet challenges can help you stay quit for good. Many people run into bumps on their journey to becoming tobacco-free.
pairs.evidence: Many people run into bumps on their journey to becoming tobacco-free. Making plans to meet these challenges will help you stay quit for good.

pairs.question: Will I gain weight after quitting smoking?
pairs.answer: Some people gain weight when they stop, but some do not. The average amount of weight gained is 7 to 10 pounds, which has little to no impact on your health.
pairs.evidence: Some people gain weight when they stop, but some do not. The average amount of weight gained, 7 to 10 pounds, has little to no impact on your health.

pairs.question: Does gaining weight affect my ability to stay quit?
pairs.answer: The amount of weight you gain has no bearing on your ability to stay quit. Staying focused on quitting is more important.
pairs.evidence: The amount of weight you gain has no bearing on your ability to stay quit—but the more worried you are about it, the more it becomes a barrier to staying quit.

pairs.question: What are some healthy snacks I can eat while quitting?
pairs.answer: You can try nibbling on low-fat snacks like carrots, fresh fruit, plain popcorn, or sugarless gum.
pairs.evidence: Some things you can try include: Nibbling on low-fat snacks such as carrots, fresh fruit, plain popcorn or sugarless gum.

pairs.question: What activities can help me stay smoke-free?
pairs.answer: Find a fun activity where smoking doesn't fit in, like jogging, walking, or even dancing.
pairs.evidence: Find a fun activity where smoking doesn't fit in, like jogging, walking or even dancing.

pairs.question: What can I do when I feel a strong urge to smoke?
pairs.answer: Urges can feel overwhelming, but they will pass in three to five minutes, whether you use or not. You can call or text a friend to distract you or leave the situation that triggers the urge.
pairs.evidence: Although urges can feel overwhelming it can help to know that urges will pass in three to five minutes, whether you use or not. Simple things you can do to prepare for urges and cravings: Call or text a friend and ask them to distract you for a few minutes. Leave the situation that gives you the urge.

pairs.question: How can I manage cravings while trying to quit?
pairs.answer: Nicotine replacement or other quit medications can help lessen the intensity of urges and cravings. It's important to have tools to manage these feelings as part of your quit plan.
pairs.evidence: Nicotine replacement or other quit medications can help lessen the intensity of urges and cravings.

pairs.question: How long do withdrawal symptoms last?
pairs.answer: Most withdrawal symptoms will lessen and finally go away as you get used to not using, typically subsiding in about two weeks. Quit medications can be very helpful during this time.
pairs.evidence: These symptoms will lessen and finally go away as you get used to not using. Most symptoms subside in about two weeks.

pairs.question: What should I do if I'm feeling irritable after quitting?
pairs.answer: Feeling grouchy, irritable, nervous, or pushy is common after quitting. These symptoms will lessen as you adjust to not using.
pairs.evidence: You may also be grouchy, irritable, nervous or pushy. These symptoms will lessen and finally go away as you get used to not using.

pairs.question: Is it okay to avoid certain situations while quitting?
pairs.answer: Yes, it's a good idea to avoid situations that trigger your urges, like parties where alcohol is served, until you feel more confident in your quit plan.
pairs.evidence: For example, being at a party where alcohol is served may make you want to use. You could walk around the block or better yet, avoid these kinds of situations until you feel more confident.

pairs.question: Should I talk to my doctor about quitting medications?
pairs.answer: Absolutely! It's important to talk with your healthcare provider to see if quit medications are right for you, especially to help with recovery symptoms.
pairs.evidence: Talk with your healthcare provider to see if medication is right for you.

pairs.question: Are there medications that can help me quit smoking?
pairs.answer: Yes, quit medications are very helpful for recovery symptoms. Talk with your healthcare provider to see if medication is right for you.
pairs.evidence: Quit medications are very helpful for recovery symptoms. Talk with your healthcare provider to see if medication is right for you.

pairs.question: Is quitting smoking really that hard?
pairs.answer: Yes, the work of quitting is important and difficult. Breaking an addiction is no small feat, so be kind to yourself.
pairs.evidence: The work of quitting is important and difficult. Be kind to yourself during your quit journey. You are trying to break an addiction and that's no small feat!

pairs.question: What if I feel irritable while trying to quit?
pairs.answer: You may feel irritable or short-tempered, even with friends and family. Know that this will pass, and you'll feel like your usual self soon.
pairs.evidence: In addition to physical symptoms, you may feel irritable or short-tempered, even with well-meaning friends and family. Know that this will pass and that you'll be back to feeling like your usual self soon.

pairs.question: How can I celebrate my progress while quitting?
pairs.answer: Take time to celebrate even small milestones. Set small and larger goals, and reward yourself when you achieve them.
pairs.evidence: Take time to celebrate even small milestones during your journey to quit. Set small and then larger goals for milestones like a day tobacco-free, a week tobacco-free and so on then reward yourself when you achieve them.

pairs.question: What are some ideas for rewards after quitting?
pairs.answer: Some ideas for rewards include downloading new music, an afternoon at the movies, a new book, or a night out on the town. Celebrating helps you stay on track.
pairs.evidence: Some ideas for rewards include downloading new music, an afternoon at the movies, a new book and a night out on the town.
